title: POC Weekly Sync - Throughput Optimization
summary: Weekly POC sync to review throughput benchmarks and tuning from last sprint. Team reviewed continuous batching gains, concurrency targets, queueing behavior and discussed next config changes and A/B runs. Action items: run 8-hour soak at target concurrency, share updated benchmark sheet, and validate KV cache warm-up on dedicated nodes.
action_items: Maya Singh - run 8-hour soak test at concurrency=60, report percentile latencies - due 2025-10-07
Diego Ramos - update benchmark sheet with new run configs and attach latency histograms - due 2025-10-03
Tom Becker - validate cache warm-up script on Dedicated nodes, log cold vs warm p50/p95 - due 2025-10-06
Claire Huang - share security docs and KMS integration notes, schedule security follow-up if needed - due 2025-10-04
next_steps: Run production-like soak at target concurrency and capture 1h/4h/8h slices
Diego to publish updated benchmark spreadsheet (link in chat)
Validate queue size and batch window settings in staging, then roll to pilot Dedicated pool
Confirm SSO/KMS requirements for Private deployment if pilot moves forward
meeting_header: Date: 2025-10-01T15:00Z | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Claire Huang (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (BlueCart), Tom Becker (BlueCart), Jin Park (BlueCart), Liam O'Connor (BlueCart)
transcript:
[00:00] Claire Huang: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off in a minute. Um Maya, Tom, is this still a good time?
[00:06] Maya Singh: Yep all good, thanks Claire.
[00:12] Claire Huang: Cool. Quick agenda: go over the throughput runs you did last week, dig into continuous batching numbers, talk concurrency/queueing targets, then action items. Diego will walk the numbers.
[00:25] Diego Ramos: Awesome, I'll share my screen - ok first slide, sorry if transcript auto missed some words but the bench sheet link is in the chat: https://redwood.ai/poc/benchmarks-sheet (note: placeholder). So we ran three key experiments: baseline (no batching), CB on with batch_window_ms=20, and CB+queueing with target_concurrency=60.
[00:44] Tom Becker: Quick Q - baseline was hosted API right? Or Dedicated?
[00:49] Diego Ramos: Baseline was hosted dev pool, single replica. The CB runs we ran on a Dedicated-like instance (same GPU type) to mimic pilot capacity.
[00:58] Maya Singh: The spreadsheet shows big gains, but the p95 tail seems to jump at higher concurrency, can you walk that?
[01:05] Diego Ramos: Yep, so raw throughput (tokens/sec) improved ~2.8x with continuous batching. p50 went down a touch, p95 improved initially but at concurrency above ~80 we saw p99 spikes from queuing pressure. With target_concurrency=60 the p95 stayed within SLA (under 300ms additional), and per-token cost decreased ~40%.
[01:30] Priya Nair: One thing we saw - KV cache warm-up matters. Cold starts push p95 up even with CB. We added a prefilling step and that smoothed the tail.
[01:41] Jin Park: Can you explain the queueing behavior? We saw some request timeouts in our simulator.
[01:47] Diego Ramos: Sure - we introduced a small ingress queue to absorb bursts and then let CB aggregate. If the queue length is too small, requests get pushed to the backend immediately causing small batches and higher per-token cost. If it's too large, you raise latency. We tuned queue_size=300 and batch_window_ms=20 as a good compromise for your workload shape.
[02:12] Claire Huang: To be clear - the recommended pilot config is: Dedicated pool, target_concurrency=60, continuous_batching on with batch_window_ms=20, queue_size=300, prefill KV cache during scale up. We'll validate with an 8-hour soak.
[02:26] Liam O'Connor: How do these numbers change if we use a quantized model? We're looking at int8 variants too.
[02:32] Diego Ramos: Quantization helps CPU/GPU memory footprint and can boost throughput 10-20% depending on model but sometimes slightly increases latency variance. We recommended running an A/B with quantized variant in the Dedicated pool, same concurrency.
[02:46] Tom Becker: Any thoughts on how the routing/fallback will affect this? If we route to cheaper model for low-priority requests will that reduce contention?
[02:54] Priya Nair: Yes, routing low-priority traffic to a smaller model or time-limited path reduces pressure and improves SLOs for high-priority traffic. In the pilot we can tag requests and route by policy. We demoed that in the last run - it worked well.
[03:08] Maya Singh: Security check - we need to confirm KMS integration and retention policies before we send any PII to pilot. Claire?
[03:14] Claire Huang: Absolutely. I'll send the SOC2 + KMS integration notes and the Private deployment checklist. If you need an on-prem package we'll loop in our security lead.
[03:23] Jin Park: Also need audit logs for inference calls at token level. Is that available?
[03:28] Claire Huang: Yes, Console has token-level cost/latency breakdowns and audit logs. We'll share the retention options.
[03:35] Diego Ramos: Back to numbers - the soak we ran for 2 hours at concurrency=60 showed steady throughput with p95 under 300ms above baseline, p99 under 800ms except during a 3-minute burst where the queue overflowed then we tuned queue_size up 20% and it handled the spike.
[03:56] Tom Becker: That overflow correlated with a scheduled CI job in our sim that spiked traffic. We'll exclude that in production sim.
[04:03] Diego Ramos: Good call. For the 8-hour soak we recommend: 1) run with production traffic mix, 2) include KV prefill on scale events, 3) compare quantized vs full precision model, 4) capture 1h/4h/8h percentiles.
[04:20] Maya Singh: On instrumentation - what do we need to add on our side to get the histograms?
[04:24] Priya Nair: Just enable request tracing headers we shared last week and the SDK will emit per-request data to the Console. We'll add the filters to the dashboard.
[04:33] Claire Huang: Next, quick discussion on concurrency target. Why 60?
[04:37] Diego Ramos: It's based on GPU model footprint, average token length, and observed batch sizes. At concurrency=60 the runtime keeps the GPU saturated with large-ish batches (~size 48-64) while keeping batch latency low. Above 80 we see diminishing returns and tail spikes.
[04:54] Jin Park: Could autoscaling handle bursts instead of queueing?
[04:58] Priya Nair: Autoscaling helps but scaling GPUs takes minutes; queueing smooths sub-minute bursts and keeps unit cost lower. A hybrid approach is what we recommend: fast ingress queue + continuous batching for steady-state, autoscale for sustained increases.
[05:13] Maya Singh: For the Dedicated pilot, what's the expected cost delta? We need a rough estimate.
[05:18] Claire Huang: From the runs, cost per 1M tokens dropped ~40% with CB at target concurrency compared to baseline hosted runs. Dedicated has a different cost model (reserved capacity) but per-token economics look better if you hit steady throughput. We'll send a cost worksheet.
[05:30] Tom Becker: Action item - Diego will publish the updated sheet with the annotated runs.
[05:34] Diego Ramos: Yep will do today, link in chat.
[05:38] Liam O'Connor: Any concerns with data residency for EU traffic?
[05:40] Claire Huang: If you need EU-only processing we can route to EU regions or spin up a Private instance; we'll note that for the security thread.
[05:48] Maya Singh: One last question - how deterministic is CB? Will it reorder requests or change latency for specific records? We have strict SLAs for some endpoints.
[05:56] Priya Nair: CB is deterministic in ordering at ingress level - we don't reorder within a request id. But batching aggregates multiple requests into same kernel call which can change relative completion times; for strict per-request latency SLAs you can mark those high-priority and route them through a low-latency path or reserve capacity.
[06:15] Claire Huang: Alright, let's recap next steps and owners. Diego publishes sheet and histograms, Maya runs the 8-hour soak at concurrency=60, Tom validates cache warm-up, Claire sends security/KMS docs. We'll reconvene next Thursday same time to review soak results.
[06:31] Maya Singh: Sounds good, thanks all.
[06:34] Tom Becker: Thanks.
[06:36] Claire Huang: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
[06:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Auto-transcript had a few mis-attributions and occasional word swaps for product names (e.g., KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K V cash") and some timestamps rounded; refer to benchmark sheet for authoritative numbers.
